title: Problem Overview
content: Erdős Problem #441 asks for the maximum size g(N) of A ⊆ {1,...,N} such that lcm(a,b) ≤ N for all a,b ∈ A. Erdős proposed a specific construction and asked if it is optimal. Answer: NO (Chen-Dai, 2006). The asymptotic is g(N) ~ (9N/8)^{1/2}.
mathContext: Define $g(N) = \max\{|A| : A \subseteq \{1,\ldots,N\},\; \mathrm{lcm}(a,b) \leq N\; \forall a,b \in A\}$. Erdős' construction uses $\{1,\ldots,\lfloor\sqrt{N/2}\rfloor\} \cup \{2k : \sqrt{N/2} \leq 2k \leq \sqrt{2N}\}$. Chen (1998) proved $g(N) \sim \sqrt{9N/8}$, and Chen-Dai (2006) showed the construction is not optimal for infinitely many $N$.

title: IsLCMBounded
content: A ⊆ {1,...,N} is LCM-bounded if all elements are in [1,N] and lcm(a,b) ≤ N for all a,b ∈ A. This restricts which pairs can coexist — elements with many common factors work well together.
mathContext: The LCM constraint $\mathrm{lcm}(a,b) = ab/\gcd(a,b) \leq N$ is equivalent to $ab \leq N \cdot \gcd(a,b)$. Elements with large GCD can have larger product while satisfying the bound. This multiplicative structure distinguishes the problem from additive extremal problems.

title: g(N) - Maximum Size
content: g(N) = max{|A| : A is LCM-bounded in {1,...,N}} is the central quantity. Erdős' question asks for its exact value and whether his construction achieves it.
mathContext: The function $g(N)$ is defined using $\texttt{sSup}$ (supremum of a set of natural numbers). The set $\{|A| : A \text{ is LCM-bounded}\}$ is finite and non-empty (contains $\{1\}$), so the supremum is attained. Computing $g(N)$ exactly for large $N$ requires exhaustive search over exponentially many subsets.

title: Erdős' Construction
content: Erdős' proposed construction: (1) all integers in [1, (N/2)^{1/2}], (2) all EVEN integers in [(N/2)^{1/2}, (2N)^{1/2}]. Small integers have small LCMs with each other; even integers in the second range have LCMs bounded by their product divided by 2.
mathContext: First part: $\{1, \ldots, \lfloor\sqrt{N/2}\rfloor\}$ has $\sim \sqrt{N/2}$ elements. For $a \leq \sqrt{N/2}$ and $b \leq N$, $\mathrm{lcm}(a,b) \leq ab \leq N$. Second part: even $2k$ with $\sqrt{N/2} \leq 2k \leq \sqrt{2N}$; for two such $2k, 2l$: $\mathrm{lcm}(2k,2l) \leq 2kl \leq N$. Cross terms: for $a \leq \sqrt{N/2}$ and $2k$ even, $\mathrm{lcm}(a, 2k) \leq 2ak \leq 2\sqrt{N/2} \cdot \sqrt{2N}/1 \leq N$.

title: ErdosQuestion
content: The main question: Is g(N) = |ErdosConstruction(N)| for all N ≥ 1? Does Erdős' construction always achieve the maximum?
mathContext: Formalized as $\forall N \geq 1: g(N) = |\text{ErdosConstruction}(N)|$. This is a universal statement asking optimality for every $N$. The answer NO means there exist specific values where strictly larger LCM-bounded sets exist by exploiting GCD structure beyond what the two-part construction captures.

title: Chen's Asymptotic (1998)
content: Chen's theorem: g(N) ~ (9N/8)^{1/2} as N → ∞. This establishes the asymptotic behavior — the construction gives the right order of magnitude.
mathContext: Chen (1998) proved $g(N)/\sqrt{9N/8} \to 1$ as $N \to \infty$, formalized as $\forall \epsilon > 0, \exists N_0, \forall N \geq N_0: |g(N)/\sqrt{9N/8} - 1| < \epsilon$. This confirms Erdős' construction gives the correct leading term $\sqrt{9N/8} \approx 1.061\sqrt{N}$.

title: Chen-Dai Upper Bound (2007)
content: Chen-Dai upper bound: g(N) ≤ (9N/8)^{1/2} + O((N/log N)^{1/2} · log log N). The error term grows with N, leaving room for the construction to be suboptimal.
mathContext: The bound $g(N) \leq \sqrt{9N/8} + C\sqrt{N/\log N} \cdot \log\log N$ has error $O(\sqrt{N/\log N} \cdot \log\log N) = o(\sqrt{N})$ but $\omega(1)$. The gap between the construction size $\sqrt{9N/8} + O(1)$ and the upper bound allows counterexamples where $g(N)$ exceeds the construction by $O(\sqrt{N/\log N})$.

title: Construction Not Optimal (Chen-Dai 2006)
content: Chen-Dai (2006): For infinitely many N, g(N) > |ErdosConstruction(N)|. This definitively answers Erdős' question: NO, the construction is not always optimal.
mathContext: $\forall M, \exists N > M: g(N) > |\text{ErdosConstruction}(N)|$ shows infinitely many counterexamples. The proof identifies $N$ values where integers with favorable GCD structure (e.g., highly composite numbers with many divisors) create strictly larger LCM-bounded sets than the rigid two-part construction allows.

title: erdos_question_disproved
content: Erdős' question is disproved: if the construction is not optimal for infinitely many N, then it cannot be optimal for ALL N. The proof is basic logic using omega.
mathContext: The proof extracts $N > 0$ from $\texttt{ConstructionNotOptimal}$ with $g(N) > |\text{Construction}(N)|$, obtains $g(N) = |\text{Construction}(N)|$ from $\texttt{ErdosQuestion}$, and derives a contradiction via `omega` ($x > y \wedge x = y \to \bot$). This is one of the fully-proved theorems in the file.
